title: Beyond the outer planes
audit_comment: BEYOND THE OUTER PLANES, printed p. 116, the closing essay of the Manual of the Planes: the preceding pages a summary of the known realms, layers and planes - by no means the final word, for the nature of these infinite realms defies any all-encompassing treatise. There can be any number of realms in a layer, so a third or fourth major pantheon can exist in Olympus/Arvandor, or a DM-created evil power can dominate a section of the Nine Hells where no arch-devils rule. Further layers may lie beyond those discovered: an eighth heaven, a third paradise unreachable by known spells and abilities, and Gladsheim perhaps with as many layers as the Abyss but without the Abyssal method of reaching them. The conception of the planes has grown with the AD&D game - the original inner planes with no mention of the quasi- and para-elemental planes, the early outer-plane discussions leaving out Concordant Opposition - and more such planes may exist beyond the scope of the model. There may also be a different form of Astral space between the outer planes and planes farther out, or within the center of Concordant Opposition. Even without new planes, the wild unexplored known lands suffice for years: the Ethereal's floating demi-planes may be world-sized, finite where the others are infinite, and the alternate Prime Material planes run Earth-like or not-so-Earth-like, familiar, hostile, and strange - the only limitation to planar adventures the imagination of those involved, the tome's purpose to fire the imaginations of DMs and players toward the myriad planes of the AD&D system.

bools.name: ddtBeyondDoctrine
bools.comment: the closing doctrine: the preceding pages are a summary of the realms, layers and planes that make up the known planes of existence - by no means the final word, for the nature of these infinite realms defies any all-encompassing treatise; there can be any number of realms in a layer, so that a third or fourth major pantheon can exist in Olympus/Arvandor, or an evil power created by the DM can dominate a section of the Nine Hells where no arch-devils rule.

bools.name: ddtUndiscoveredLayers
bools.comment: the undiscovered layers: it is also possible there are further layers beyond those discovered and reported - there may be an eighth heaven, or a third paradise, undiscovered or unreachable by the spells and abilities known to researchers; and Gladsheim may have as many layers as the Abyss, but lacks the Abyssal method of reaching them.

bools.name: ddtGrowingModel
bools.comment: the growing model: our conception of the planes has grown with the AD&D game - the original presentations of the inner planes make no mention of the quasi- and para-elemental planes, and the early discussions of the outer planes leave out Concordant Opposition; there may be more such planes beyond the scope of the model presented here.

bools.name: ddtNewAstralForms
bools.comment: the new Astral forms: there may be a different form of Astral space between the outer planes and planes farther out, or within the center of Concordant Opposition - the map not being the territory, and the void between the wheels its own country.

bools.name: ddtDemiPlaneRule
bools.comment: the demi-plane rule: even without new planes, the wild and unexplored known lands can occupy the extraplanar traveler for years - the demi-planes that float in the Ethereal may be the size of worlds, their only limitation that they are finite where the other planes are infinite.

bools.name: ddtAlternatePrimeRule
bools.comment: the alternate Prime rule: alternate Prime Material planes enable travelers to visit worlds that are Earth-like or not-so-Earth-like, familiar, hostile, and strange - the only limitation to planar adventures being the imagination of those involved; the purpose of the tome is to fire the imaginations of DMs and players so that they explore the myriad planes of the AD&D system.
